subject: Next Steps: Sherwood architecture & observability checklist
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@sherwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next Steps: Sherwood architecture & observability checklist

Hi Alex — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the architecture/POC work. I copied Marissa (SE) and Karthik (Infra) for technical follow-ups.

Summary from today's call
- Sherwood will evaluate Redwood for: hosted + private dedicated lanes for latency-sensitive inference, embeddings-based semantic search with reranking, and tool-calling for structured actions.
- Key non-functional asks: trace propagation across frontend -> Redwood -> downstream services, consistent request IDs in logs, and 99th-percentile latency visibility per model/pipeline.

Proposed immediate next steps (owner — due):
1) Integration checklist & mutual action plan — Rachel (me) — 2027-04-09: I attached a working checklist (redwood-sherwood-integration-checklist.xlsx) with sections for SDK auth, network, and policy gating.
2) SE workshop: SDK auth + routing + structured output — Marissa — 2027-04-12: 90-minute session (we'll bring code snippets for SDK init, token rotation, and example tool-calling payloads).
3) Observability plan: trace IDs, logging fields, latency headers — Karthik — 2027-04-14: provide header names, example middleware, and a sample dashboard.
4) Security & compliance Qs (KMS/SOC2 logs) — Alex to introduce security contact (Priya) — 2027-04-08: need retention window + KMS requirements.

Observability specifics we propose (initial):
- Trace ID propagation: use X-Trace-ID header (we also echo it in response headers as X-RW-TRACE).
- Request ID + log fields: include redwood.request_id and redwood.model_version in structured logs forwarded to your aggregator (we can map to your field names).
- Latency breakdown headers: X-RW-LATENCY-ms: pre-processing|queue|inference|post-processing (ms)
- Sampling keys: percent-based sampling for p99 tracing; configurable per route.
- Dashboards: per-model token throughput, 95/99 latency, cache-hit ratio (for KV/prefix caching).

Attachments & links: integration checklist (attached), proposed MA P link and HubSpot deal (links below).

Questions for Sherwood before the SE session:
- Do you prefer API-key auth for the POC or mutual mTLS? Any corporate SSO requirement?
- Which logging/monitoring stack will receive our structured logs (Splunk/Datadog/Elk)?
- Approx expected QPS for embeddings vs. generation?

I'll schedule the SE workshop for the week of Apr 12; please reply with preferred times and Priya's contact for SOC2/infra questions.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

--
Attachment: redwood-sherwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@sherwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@sherwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next Steps: Sherwood architecture & observability checklist

Thanks Rachel — helpful recap. Priya (cc'd) is our security lead and will own the SOC2/KMS questions. A few clarifications from our side:

- We prefer mTLS for Dedicated (production) but API-key or OAuth for the initial POC is OK.
- Our logging stack is Datadog (we send JSON logs from services). We will want a small schema to map redwood.request_id -> trace_id so everything can be connected in traces.
- QPS targets: embeddings (50–100 q/s), generator endpoints (30–40 q/s) with peak bursts to 150 q/s for short periods.

I've attached a simple network diagram for our VPC and where the Dedicated instances would sit (sherwood-network-diagram.pdf) — please have your infra team review port requirements and NAT/VPN needs.

Two asks for the SE workshop:
1) please include a short demo of embedding + reranker flow (end-to-end) — we want to see how to supply candidate embeddings and call the reranker.
2) show an example of structured tool-calling where the model returns a JSON payload we can safely parse and pass to our orchestration layer.

We're available Apr 12 afternoon PT or Apr 13 morning PT.

—Alex
Alex Barnes
Head of Platform Engineering, Sherwood AI
alex.barnes@sherwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0104

Attachment: sherwood-network-diagram.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@sherwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 12:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next Steps: Sherwood architecture & observability checklist

Alex / Rachel — quick note from the SE side ahead of the workshop:

Observability + SDK details we'll cover (short bullets):
- SDK init: token refresh + example for node/python (we'll provide a sample repo).
- Auth: show API-key rotation approach and mutual TLS config (example openssl commands + cert rotation notes).
- Trace header & response echo: we plan to use X-Trace-ID inbound; Redwood will set X-RW-TRACE on responses and include redwood.request_id and redwood.model_version in structured logs. We'll also emit a header X-RW-INVOCATION that contains a small UUID for cross-system joins.
- Latency breakdown format: we'll return X-RW-LATENCY-ms with four pipe-delimited values (pre|queue|inference|post). Example: X-RW-LATENCY-ms: 2|5|24|1
- Embeddings + reranker: we'll walk through candidate embedding batch formats (ndarray/jsonlines), and provide a sample reranker call that takes an embedding id list + context.
- Structured output: show JSON schema enforcement with a 'type' field and an example tool-calling handshake (signature verification + size limits).

Action items for workshop prep (we'll own these):
- Send sample SDK snippet and a small repo link (Marissa) — by 2027-04-09.
- Provide a proposed Datadog dashboard JSON (Karthik) — by 2027-04-14.

I'll include runnable snippets in the repo; we can also spin up a sandbox org for Sherwood to test end-to-end.

See you on Apr 12 (afternoon PT) unless you prefer Apr 13 morning.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
